decisions.difference: A: (diagnosis Monkeypox possible)  vs  B: (active_condition Monkeypox possible) in both tasks and all probable/priority rules
decisions.reason: Same meaning; Will's briefing names (diagnosis X possible) as the form for a possible diagnosis made by another rule, for the page's 'patient with suspected mpox'.

decisions.difference: A: extra task "Check for mpox exposure, lesion sites and associated symptoms" triggered by a skin lesion/eruption or face/genital/rectal/oral/eye lesion  vs  B: no such task
decisions.final_expr: (or Skin lesion, Eruption, Lesion of face, Lesion of genitalia, Lesion of rectum, Oral lesion, Lesion of eye)
decisions.reason: "Suspect mpox if …" needs its contact, lesion and symptom findings asked; B never asks them, so its possible-mpox rule can only fire on findings recorded elsewhere.

decisions.difference: A: check_for of exposure to monkeypox virus, new lesions at each listed site, headache, sore throat, nasal congestion, cough, lymphadenopathy, aches, muscle pain, backache, severe fatigue/asthenia  vs  B: none
decisions.reason: These are the "Suspect mpox if" criteria on the page; asking them is what lets the suspicion rule fire.

decisions.difference: A: new lesion at each listed site (face, palm skin, sole skin, genitalia, anus, rectum, mouth, eye)  vs  B: (Skin lesion + New)
decisions.final_expr: (or Lesion of face New, Skin lesion@palm New, Skin lesion@sole New, Lesion of genitalia New, Skin lesion@anus New, Lesion of rectum New, Oral lesion New, Lesion of eye New)
decisions.reason: The page lists the sites in parentheses ("face, palms of hands/soles of feet, genitals, anus, rectum, mouth or eyes"), and rectum, mouth and eyes are not skin, so the site list is the closer encoding; whether the list restricts or only exemplifies is not settled by the page.

decisions.difference: A: (<= (onset exposure to Monkeypox virus) (time_ago 21 days))  vs  B: exposure with no time window
decisions.reason: Page says "in the 21 days before symptom onset"; a 21-day window measured from now is closer to that than no window (recorded under Could not model).

decisions.difference: A: Obstipation (disorder)  vs  B: Difficulty in ability to defecate (finding) for "Unable to pass … stool"
decisions.reason: Page says "unable to pass" stool; obstipation is inability to pass stool, while "difficulty" is broader; listed as a clinician question.

decisions.difference: A: Persistent vomiting only  vs  B: Nausea and Persistent vomiting
decisions.reason: Page says "Persistent nausea and vomiting", which names both.

decisions.difference: A: Persistent vomiting  vs  B: (and Nausea Persistent vomiting)
decisions.reason: Page says "Persistent nausea and vomiting", which names both.

decisions.difference: A: Leg swelling symptom  vs  B: Swelling of lower limb, for "swollen legs" (check_for and myocarditis rule)
decisions.reason: Both fit "swollen legs"; Leg swelling symptom is the form VHA rules already use (8 uses vs 1).

decisions.difference: A: Abnormal vision (finding)  vs  B: Visual disturbance (disorder), for "vision changes" (check_for and corneal infection rule)
decisions.reason: Both fit "vision changes"; Visual disturbance is the form VHA rules already use (12 uses vs 1).

decisions.difference: A: Confusional state (disorder)  vs  B: Acute confusion (finding), for "confusion" (check_for and priority)
decisions.reason: Acute confusion is VHA's Confusion warning-sign concept, so the page's "confusion" is recorded the same way everywhere.

decisions.difference: A: (and HIV known present, HIV RNA above reference range)  vs  B: not encoded, for "HIV not on ART/virologically unsuppressed"
decisions.final_expr: (and (clinical_finding HIV infection Known present) (clinical_finding Copies of HIV RNA above reference range))
decisions.reason: "Virologically unsuppressed" is expressible as a finding concept (not a lab value), so A encodes part of the page; "not on ART" stays under Could not model.

decisions.difference: A: Itching  vs  B: Itching of skin, for "itchy/non-itchy" branches (all differential rules)
decisions.reason: Page says "Itchy"/"Non-itchy" without a site; Itching is the general concept (parent of Itching of skin) and the more used VHA form.

decisions.difference: A: Localized skin lesion  vs  B: Localized eruption of skin, for "Localised rash or lesion/s"
decisions.reason: Page says "rash or lesion/s"; a skin lesion covers single lesions such as molluscum papules, which an eruption need not.

decisions.difference: A: Vesicular eruption  vs  B: Vesicle of skin, for chickenpox "crops of vesicles"
decisions.reason: "Crops of vesicles" describes an eruption of many vesicles, not a single vesicle.

decisions.difference: A: Acquired immune deficiency syndrome  vs  B: HIV infection Known present, for "advanced HIV disease"
decisions.reason: Page says "advanced" HIV disease; AIDS is closer than any known HIV infection.

decisions.difference: A: Itching + Night time qualifier  vs  B: absent, for scabies "itch worse at night"
decisions.reason: The page names "itch worse at night" as a scabies criterion and a concept for it exists.

decisions.difference: A: onset of Exposure to Drug or medicament <= 3 months  vs  B: onset of New medication commenced <= 3 months
decisions.reason: Page says "new medication in past 3 months"; New medication commenced says exactly that.

decisions.difference: A: no molluscum rule  vs  B: probable molluscum contagiosum (localised, non-itchy, firm dome-shaped papule, Skin dimple)
decisions.final_expr: (diagnosis Infection caused by Molluscum contagiosum probable)
decisions.reason: Page says "If firm, dome-shaped papules with central dimple, molluscum contagiosum likely"; Skin dimple is a usable if imperfect concept for the dimple (low confidence, clinician question).

decisions.difference: A: Pain of skin  vs  B: Pain, for "painful" (herpes simplex, hand-foot and mouth, shingles)
decisions.reason: Page says the vesicles/blisters are painful; Pain of skin keeps the pain on the skin lesion, while Pain would also match e.g. chest pain.

decisions.difference: A: grouped vesicles, no erythema  vs  B: ungrouped vesicle plus Erythema, for herpes simplex "painful, grouped vesicles on red base"
decisions.final_expr: (and Pain of skin (Vesicle of skin + Grouped) Erythema)
decisions.reason: Page says both "grouped" and "on red base"; A has the first, B the second, so the final takes both.

decisions.difference: A: palm skin / sole skin finding sites  vs  B: Hand structure / Foot structure, for hand-foot and mouth "palms and soles"
decisions.final_expr: (Vesicle of skin @ Entire skin of palmar area of hand) and (@ Entire skin of sole of foot)
decisions.reason: Page says "palms and soles"; A's body structures resolve and are exactly those sites, B's are the whole hand and foot.

decisions.difference: A: Nasal discharge in check_for  vs  B: not in check_for (measles)
decisions.reason: "Runny nose" is a measles criterion; asking it costs nothing even though it is a common symptom.

decisions.difference: A: no Lymphadenopathy in the lower task  vs  B: Lymphadenopathy in the lower task
decisions.reason: Lymphadenopathy ("swollen lymph nodes") is already asked in the suspicion task of the final build.

decisions.difference: Rule descriptions: A "Check for urgent mpox danger signs" / "Check for proctitis and other causes of rash/lesions in suspected mpox" / "Diagnose possible mpox (contact or new lesions with systemic symptoms)"  vs  B "Check for urgent mpox conditions" / "Check for other causes of rash or lesions in suspected mpox" / "Diagnose possible mpox"
decisions.reason: Naming only; A's are page-specific and unique, which descriptions must be.

notes: Both builds passed and agreed on structure (possible-mpox anchor, red-box task, approach task, 15 probable rules, one Urgent priority rule). A was the base because it asks the 'Suspect mpox if' criteria and keeps the page's lesion sites, palms/soles, night-time itch and the 21-day window. From B: Visual disturbance, Acute confusion, Nausea with persistent vomiting, New medication commenced, Erythema (red base) and the molluscum rule. Most of the 168 atom-level differences in diff.json come from the diagnosis/active_condition form and the Itching/Localized concept choices, which repeat across every differential rule; each is covered by one decision above.
